examples.text: This is suggestive that financial clout is a more determining factor in trade policy outcomes than voting power.

The discourse of the community economy thus questions the practice of singling out certain activities as necessarily or invariably more important, more independent, more determining of economic “health” and distinguishing them from those that are more expendable, dependent, and less determining or potentially destructive within the economy.

He suggested that social factors are even more determining than biological factors and emphasized that low levels of stress and high levels of social connection are more protective than not smoking, eating a good diet, and exercising regularly.

glosses: present participle and gerund of determine
Essential or decisive for determining the outcome or future of something; extremely important; vital.

examples.text: A secure supply of crude oil is crucial for any modern nation, let alone a superpower.
The battle of Tali-Ihantala in 1944 is one of the crucial moments in the history of Finland.

The perfume industry is facing a major problem: maintaining constant levels of quality is crucial, but it is increasingly difficult to obtain a regular supply of all the necessary natural ingredients.

Vocabulary provides a foundation from which grammar, phonology, and morphology emerge, and in a subject area it provides access to conceptual knowledge. Vocabulary selection for pedagogical purposes is therefore crucial.
Language is crucial because it is the best weapon against violence. When children don’t have the words to express their thoughts, they raise their fists.

glosses: Very good; excellent; particularly applied to reggae music.

examples.text: Delbert Wilkins is the most crucial pirate radio DJ in Brixton.
The more profound and consequential the issue, the more stubborn our denial.
He was a very short, fat little man, with immensely long grey side-whiskers, and a most consequential manner.

examples.text: La laïcité est engagée dans une lutte âpre et décisive contre le cléricalisme. L'État se bat contre l'Église.

Un évènement, un fait, un jugement, un moment, un rôle décisif.
Une raison, une preuve, une expérience décisive.

examples.text: Il eut tort de citer le mot de Voltaire, qui est beaucoup trop décisif et immodéré : « L’écriture est la peinture de la voix ; plus elle est ressemblante, meilleure elle est », et qui conduirait à l’orthographe individuelle, c’est-à-dire à une confusion telle qu’on ne se comprendrait jamais quand on s’écrirait les uns aux autres ; […].

examples.text: Incision cruciale.
